summary: Verified the new 'Preferiti' (favorites) feature end-to-end. Backend: 7/7 pytest tests PASS (idempotent toggle, 404 on invalid id, GET /favorites with proper ordering + no _id leak, defaults is_favorite=false, non-regression on delete/mark-viewed/delete-many). Frontend (Playwright on mobile viewport): star button renders top-right of every result card, tapping toggles between grey star-border and yellow filled star (#FFC107), star is hidden in selection mode and reappears after cancel, and the toggled state is persisted in the DB (verified via GET /api/results/favorites showing the tapped result_id). Feature is production-ready.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning on web: `useNativeDriver is not supported because the native animated module is missing. Falling back to JS-based animation.` This is expected on Expo web preview (native driver only works on iOS/Android builds) — not a bug, just noise. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/ResultCard.tsx:76-86

critical_code_review_comments: ResultCard.tsx correctly uses useEffect to sync isFavorite when result.is_favorite prop changes — good for re-fetch scenarios.

Backend toggle endpoint uses find_one + update_one which is correct but not atomic; under heavy concurrent taps on the same result_id there is a small race window. For a single-user mobile app this is acceptable; consider find_one_and_update with bitwise/aggregation pipeline if concurrency becomes an issue.
GET /api/results/favorites uses projection {_id: 0} and Pydantic serialization — safe against ObjectId leaks (verified in test).
Optimistic UI in handleToggleFavorite correctly rolls back on error and syncs to server response on success.
seed_data_creation: Created 3 temporary searches during test runs; all cleaned up by fixture teardown / DELETE calls. One user-triggered favorite (result 736be300...) was left toggled after Playwright run and manually un-toggled via curl.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_favorites.py — reuse them for regression. On web preview, MaterialIcons render as font glyphs (span text) not SVG, so if you want to detect star color programmatically use getComputedStyle().color on the icon element, or rely on visual screenshots. The star icon character is different between 'star' and 'star-border' so text content or CSS color are the reliable signals.
